過敏人口增加，過敏不只是台灣的問題

作者 Archie 從「過敏是否已成為國民病」談起，指出台灣約有四分之一人口患有過敏性鼻炎，約百分之七有異位性皮膚炎；韓國、美國也有不少兒童與成人受到過敏困擾。台灣過敏人口仍有增加趨勢，過敏已是全球普遍的健康議題，而非台灣獨有。

過敏進程與免疫系統

作者介紹過敏症狀彼此交疊的現象，稱為「過敏進程」：嬰兒可能先有異位性皮膚炎，添加副食品後出現食物過敏，幼年時可能發展為氣喘，到了青少年階段則可能出現過敏性鼻炎，且鼻炎往往持續較久。腸道與呼吸道等上皮屏障若不夠完整，外來物質便較容易進入體內，引起免疫反應。

免疫系統中的 Th1 主要對抗細胞內的病毒與細菌，Th2 則與寄生蟲及過敏原反應有關；另有 Th17 和調節型 T 細胞，分別參與對抗真菌與平息發炎。若免疫反應過度偏向Th2，身體可能更容易過敏，對其他威脅的防禦也可能失衡。作者建議有相關困擾者尋求免疫專科醫師評估。

衛生假說與環境影響

作者說明衛生假說：若兒童早期接觸微生物的機會太少，免疫系統可能更容易對塵蟎、花粉或食物等原本無害的物質產生過度反應。部分研究發現，嬰幼兒時期接觸貓狗與較低的過敏風險有關；家中有年長手足的孩子，也可能因接觸更多環境微生物而較不容易過敏。這些研究仍屬假說與相關性觀察，作者提醒不必刻意讓孩子處於髒亂環境，但適度接觸自然、避免過度無菌，可能有助免疫系統發展。

遺傳、皮膚屏障與食物致敏

過敏成因包括遺傳與環境。遺傳影響程度依疾病而異，異位性皮膚炎的遺傳比例較高；日常保濕可幫助減少輕症患者的發作，但嚴重狀況仍可能需要進一步治療。皮膚屏障受損也是重要因素，尤其是異位性皮膚炎患者，外來過敏原較容易穿過皮膚，引發免疫反應。

作者進一步說明皮膚致敏的觀念：嬰兒可能尚未吃過某種食物，卻因皮膚受損時接觸到食物殘留或微粒而產生致敏反應，例如花生粉塵沾到皮膚，可能促使身體形成花生特異性抗體。作者也提到，美國氣候較乾燥，皮膚屏障更容易乾裂，可能增加食物微粒經皮膚接觸的機會；因此，維持皮膚屏障與適當保濕，是理解及照護過敏的重要一環。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 從育兒家庭的日常細節，呈現孩子出生後伴侶如何因忙碌與疲憊而逐漸疏遠。
  • 坦誠探討「育兒孤單」、缺乏伴侶交流，以及關係中親密感減少等不容易啟齒的問題。
  • 分享可實際嘗試的相處方式，也帶出臨時托育對父母身心健康的重要性。

摘要

育兒讓關係更像家人，卻少了浪漫

作者與伴侶聊起有孩子之後的生活。他們認為，兩人的關係確實有所改善，但更多是成為朋友、夥伴與家人；相較之下，戀愛感與浪漫親密卻逐漸減少。作者也提到，多數伴侶在有孩子後關係會變得更緊張，而離婚率下降未必代表感情更好，也可能只是離婚變得更加複雜。

忙碌日常幾乎沒有喘息空間

孩子出生後，家務、照料、生病與睡眠不足接踵而來，孩子的作息和需求也不斷改變。作者描述他們的一天：清晨起床、送孩子上學、工作、接孩子回家，再忙著餵食、做家事和哄睡。等孩子終於入睡，一人往往已陪睡到睡著，另一人則還要收拾家裡、處理工作，兩人的作息因此幾乎錯開。

只剩下交代事情，缺少真正的交流

兩人能相處的時間，通常只剩通勤和工作午餐；即使見面，談的也多是工作、拍片計畫或孩子需要什麼。忙碌時，彼此的對話甚至只剩「幫忙拿東西」或交代下一件事，難有深入交流。作者的朋友聽了他們幾乎沒有相處時間的情況後感到驚訝，也讓作者更清楚看見伴侶之間的疏離。

孤單與關係疏遠的可能性

作者認為，當伴侶長期缺乏有品質的相處，生活圈又各自分開，人在外界獲得關心與陪伴時，便可能更容易和伴侶以外的人建立親密連結。這不一定是感情變了，也可能是伴侶之間缺少共同時間與情感交流。為了改善狀況，他們開始在孩子睡著後叫醒陪睡的人，讓兩人還有機會聊天、處理事情，而不是一睡到深夜才醒來。

育兒孤單與喘息時間的重要

作者談到「育兒孤單」不只是獨自照顧孩子，也包含無法做自己、無法和朋友或伴侶好好相處。她認為，每週若能有幾小時臨時托育，讓父母喘口氣，對身心健康十分重要。他們目前會趁孩子在健身房托育區玩耍時運動、游泳，哪怕只有短短一段時間，也能感到放鬆。影片最後開始提及，在美國，沒有孩子的人或許也會感受到另一種孤單，但相關討論在字幕中未完整呈現。

Exactly , this situation is actually really poor . Why? Look, our schedules have almost no overlapping free time. You can’t exactly be romantic before the kids go to sleep, right? You’re definitely busy with the kids, so how could there be. time for romance? So, what time do we actually have left to spend together? Only two times: the commute between the office and home, and having lunch together at work. That’s our only time together, and when we have lunch at the office, other friends usually join us, so it’s more like a casual chat with friends. During our commute, what do we usually talk about? We talk about the YouTube business, like what we’re filming this weekend, what we need to prepare, or our podcast topics, so when would we ever have time to be romantic? On top of that. , if things get busy, Chang-jen often has meetings during lunch or while we're commuting in the car. This week, for instance, he was so busy that I felt like I really didn't talk to you at all. >> We obviously have some verbal communication, like asking each other to grab something or discussing what the kids need, but we never talk about anything beyond these "orders." It’s always just telling each other what to do next, with no chance for real conversation. So, we actually had a chance before when my mom was here; I let Chang-jen and my mom watch the kids.

while I went out with some female friends, and we brought up this topic. How did you feel during that time out? >> Of course, I was happy. Going out with friends is naturally fun, but we ended up talking a lot about how we have absolutely no meaningful interaction between us. They were truly shocked, saying, "Wow, if you have no time together like that, how can you even call yourselves partners?"...that way, because they don't have kids yet, they just can't really understand this situation. So, I really don't find infidelity surprising at all. Personally , I can't really fathom it because I'm too busy with life; I don't have time. for an affair. But since we work at the same company, we still have our commute and our lunch breaks to spend time together. If we worked at different companies, how many words unrelated to work would we actually say to each other in a day, right? Besides talking about household matters, maybe not even a single word. In that case, if I were working overtime and some handsome male colleague were there checking in on me and being sweet, it would actually be pretty understandable to have an affair , right? I personally don't have the energy for it, but I think I can kind of grasp why so many people say it's really. easy to cheat after middle age. I don't think it's because people's hearts have changed, but rather because it's genuinely hard to have any quality overlap in your social circles, so you end up spending time with other people instead. To improve this, we now make sure to wake up the person who falls asleep with the kids. Whether it's me or you, we make sure to wake the person up around nine o'clock once we feel the kids are asleep. >> Because if you wake them up right when they're nodding off, you still have the rest of the night to get things done or just chat or whatever.

Otherwise, falling asleep at nine really tanks your productivity; it means you can't get anything else done for the day , like chores or anything else. It's impossible to wake up at one or two in the morning and feel like cleaning the house. Usually, you don't have the motivation for that; you'll just end up mindlessly scrolling on your phone. So, I actually relate quite a bit to the concept of "parenting loneliness." This "parenting loneliness"—when Shen Bo was running for mayor of Taipei, he proposed some welfare policies, suggesting that we should give young parents a few hours.

# 育兒孤單

of childcare so they can take a break, because it's so easy for parents to end up with no friends. Of course, that resonated with so many people, because parenting loneliness doesn't just mean you're parenting by yourself; it means you can't be yourself, and you can't have quality interactions with your friends or partner, which I think is a completely, absolutely normal thing. So I think having a few hours of temporary childcare a week is really, really important for parents, and crucial for them to maintain their own physical and mental well-being. Our current solution. is going to the gym. Every time we go, we can drop the kids off for two hours, though we usually can't leave them that long. We let them play in there for an hour while we exercise, and then we go swimming together. Even though it’s only an hour of free time, it’s the only time we really feel we can actually get a workout in. The workout feels especially great, >> like getting some time off, >> Right, exactly. Honestly, if I didn't have to work, I’d want to go more often . And actually, in the US, compared to.

the loneliness of parenting, it’s perhaps even easier to feel the loneliness of not having kids. Because once you’re around 40, if you don't have children, it’s easy to feel like you have no friends, since friends stop asking you to hang out because they all have families. So, the fertility rate among your social circle really affects your desire to have kids, but even if your friends do have them, if the age gap is too big, it can still be quite difficult. For example, I have a very close friend who chose to have kids—not necessarily due to age, but the birth. year of her child was much earlier than the others—so she spent about four or five years stuck in that sense of parenting loneliness. Then, once our friends started having kids one after another, we could finally hang out again , though it’s still tough if the age gaps are wide, because group parenting with kids of similar ages is truly amazing. >> It’s really great. >> So relaxing. >> The things they interact with and want to do are similar, so you can actually handle two or three kids on your own. >> Right, exactly, you could even have one person watch four or five kids while the.

other parents scroll on their phones and relax. That kind of group parenting is something we really love. >> Usually, we just chat and whatnot. >> Right, exactly, just having that. So, we try to meet up with people who have kids of similar ages almost every weekend, but finally, let me think, the Lindsay Clancy case—that one is very famous. A mother suffering from severe postpartum depression sent her husband away, killed her three children, and then tried to jump to her death, but she survived and ended up in prison.

# 美國慘案

A while back, her trial sparked a lot of discussion in the US. I don't want to debate her guilt today, because the fact that she killed her child is clear. Whether she's guilty is a legal matter. What I want to discuss is why she resonated with so many American women. Raising children in the US is genuinely difficult, and it can be incredibly lonely during those initial stages. The American social system often leaves parents on their own because daycare is mostly very expensive. It’s 2,000 dollars a month where we are, and in big. cities like DC, it might be 3,000 dollars. Some states are better—I know New York has free daycare—but most places don't. So if you're a middle-income woman, once you have two kids, your salary simply won't cover daycare. You know, so quitting your job becomes a very, very logical choice, even if you’ve spent so many years studying. It’s not easy to build a career you love and feel like things are finally stable , only to have to give up everything you’ve worked for the moment you have a child. Plus, they don't have our culture.

of having elders help out, so new mothers often have to face this all on their own. So, you can imagine that when you're physically exhausted after childbirth and can’t even get a good night's sleep, you have to take care of an even more fragile infant. Your life is completely stripped away, and you might look messy and disheveled every day. You won't want to face your glamorous friends, so you enter a very lonely state, which makes it really easy to fall into depression. Our company actually encourages new parents to get to know one another, and the way Europe. encourages this follows the same logic— it’s all about providing new parents with more emotional support. Our conclusion for today is that it's actually very reasonable for a couple's romantic relationship to cool off after having children. Our relationship has improved, but that improvement feels more like we've become partners and family, rather than just romantic lovers . To be honest, raising kids isn't easy . Once they're sound asleep around 9 PM and I’m working alone until 11 or 12, I’ll open Facebook and get pushed all these short videos aimed at middle-aged women, you know?

# 結語

I’ve talked about this before; they target middle-aged moms like me as their audience. Even though I don't like watching them, I see so many, and most are romance-related, some even a bit R-rated . I truly understand why middle-aged women might want to cheat or have certain emotional needs. When I look at my husband snoring beside me and think about the dishes I just finished, I think, "Yeah, this all makes perfect sense." >> Could you wake me up, please? >> Our relationship has improved, so I want you to get more rest, but I do think that makes total sense. >> I’d still prefer you to wake me up, otherwise the whole night is just wasted . That’s true; if I want you to get more done, I really have to wake you up. Finally, I often share snippets of my parenting life on Instagram Stories. Many times, it's just really messy photos, but they get tons of views, and I get so many DMs saying, "Oh, I love seeing this kind of realistic parenting ." All that "elegant parenting" stuff just stresses me out. Seeing someone. else struggling like me makes me feel at ease. I don’t share more not because I’m self-conscious, but because I have no time to take photos. Like right now, someone is already on the floor. Then the other one is already asleep, and my phone is way across the room, so I can't take pictures to show you guys. Alright , that’s all for today. I’m A-Chi. >> I’m Ching-Shang-Chien. See you next time , bye-bye.

item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AAJ_Kuoawu0

值得閱讀的理由

  • 呈現三代同堂的日常分工，分享如何依照長輩的喜好相處，避免彼此勉強。
  • 記錄外婆陪伴孩子、協助家務的生活點滴，既溫馨又充滿幽默。
  • 帶領讀者感受美國秋日風景，從農場、南瓜到萬聖節活動，體驗當地季節氣氛。

摘要

三代同堂，各自分工

作者分享，母親已在家中住了兩個月，這段相處不是「血淚史」，而是溫馨的生活紀錄。作者認為有孩子後，三代同堂很值得推薦；不過，母親並不喜歡下廚或做家事，因此相處的關鍵是因材施教，按照她能接受的方式分配事情，不必要求她做不擅長、也不喜歡的工作。

平日早上，母親會陪孩子，白天則幫忙洗切蔬菜、整理碗盤、接孩子放學並帶他們出門玩。作者下班後只要專心準備晚餐，家務就能順利完成。作者打趣說，母親簡直像家中的「小幫手」，一家人各做各的，日子過得更有效率。

外婆陪玩，家人也心疼她

母親常帶孩子到公園散步、騎三輪車，還會陪他們放學後到處走走。孩子玩得開心，母親卻經常一出去就是一個多小時，甚至晚餐都準備好了還沒回家。作者和伴侶笑說，孩子已經懂得什麼時候可以使喚外婆，也擔心母親離開後，孩子會不習慣放學就直接回家。

為了慰勞辛苦散步回家的母親，家人準備了她喜歡的起司拼盤，還拿出幽靈、南瓜和蝙蝠造型的小叉子增添節日氣氛。母親回家後，作者也提醒孩子要體諒外婆，不能一直賴著不肯回家。

母親愛用的廚具與難得的相聚時光

作者介紹母親最常使用的廚房用品：因為母親每天早上要吃早餐、服用藥物，所以很常使用鬆餅機的三明治烤盤，能同時烤麵包和煎蛋；她也喜歡一只外型漂亮的陶瓷鍋。那只鍋已經停產，是作者到韓國時收到的贈品，母親以前曾想帶回台灣，如今能在美國使用也很滿足。

母親難得來訪，作者盡量安排出遊，也趁有人幫忙照顧孩子時，和伴侶輪流處理積壓的工作，希望母親回去後生活能輕鬆一些。他們仍安排了幾趟附近旅行，例如到西雅圖參觀保育型動物園；園區保留大片自然環境，動物看起來像生活在野外。

追賞秋色，體驗南瓜季

母親此行最期待的是欣賞秋天的紅葉。作者一家住處周圍有各種顏色的樹葉，晴朗的天氣也讓母親每天散步都很愉快。他們走訪不同農場，讓孩子參加戶外活動，大人則在旁休息、挑選南瓜。作者一直想買南瓜裝飾家裡，這次終於趁母親同行，體驗了美國秋天的經典活動。

作者說明，秋天的南瓜不只是食物，也是重要的季節裝飾，有些品種甚至主要供擺設。家人挑選不同顏色與造型的南瓜，雖然外表不規則、看起來有點「醜」，卻很有萬聖節氣氛；這些南瓜買回家是用來裝飾，並不是打算吃掉。

萬聖節活動與孩子的裝扮難題

萬聖節前夕，當地動物園舉辦讓孩子穿著裝扮討糖的活動，作者帶母親一起參加，也展示父子倆的造型。接著，孩子學校舉行秋日慶典，附近農場也有萬聖節活動，穿著裝扮入場還能免費，因此一家人也前往參加。

作者特地準備了和孩子相配的服裝與頭飾，原本期待一家人完整變裝，沒想到孩子不願意穿，伴侶也不喜歡毛茸茸的服飾，精心準備的百元裝扮因此派不上用場。作者笑說，免費入場的吸引力很強，活動現場人潮遠比動物園更多；但為孩子挑衣服並不容易，男孩的選擇尤其有限。影片最後提到作者買了哈利波特造型服，後續內容則未在字幕中呈現。

================================================

Hi everyone, I'm A-Qi. My mom has been staying with us for two months now, so today let’s take a look at a two-month-long... Is this a memoir of blood and tears or a heartwarming one? >> A heartwarming memoir. I have to say, after having kids, I really promote living together as three generations. But actually, my mom isn't like your mom who loves cooking and doing chores. She really dislikes these things, but she tries for her daughter's sake. So, I think the secret to getting along with elders is "teaching according to their. aptitude."" >> Teaching according to aptitude" sounds like a lot of pressure. No, it's like this: my mom really doesn't like housework, but she'll still do a little . If I made her cook, she'd be stressed and I wouldn't think it tastes good either, so there's no need to torture each other. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 呈現三代同堂的日常分工，分享如何依照長輩的喜好相處，避免彼此勉強。
  • 記錄外婆陪伴孩子、協助家務的生活點滴，既溫馨又充滿幽默。
  • 帶領讀者感受美國秋日風景，從農場、南瓜到萬聖節活動，體驗當地季節氣氛。

摘要

三代同堂，各自分工

作者分享，母親已在家中住了兩個月，這段相處不是「血淚史」，而是溫馨的生活紀錄。作者認為有孩子後，三代同堂很值得推薦；不過，母親並不喜歡下廚或做家事，因此相處的關鍵是因材施教，按照她能接受的方式分配事情，不必要求她做不擅長、也不喜歡的工作。

平日早上，母親會陪孩子，白天則幫忙洗切蔬菜、整理碗盤、接孩子放學並帶他們出門玩。作者下班後只要專心準備晚餐，家務就能順利完成。作者打趣說，母親簡直像家中的「小幫手」，一家人各做各的，日子過得更有效率。

外婆陪玩，家人也心疼她

母親常帶孩子到公園散步、騎三輪車，還會陪他們放學後到處走走。孩子玩得開心，母親卻經常一出去就是一個多小時，甚至晚餐都準備好了還沒回家。作者和伴侶笑說，孩子已經懂得什麼時候可以使喚外婆，也擔心母親離開後，孩子會不習慣放學就直接回家。

為了慰勞辛苦散步回家的母親，家人準備了她喜歡的起司拼盤，還拿出幽靈、南瓜和蝙蝠造型的小叉子增添節日氣氛。母親回家後，作者也提醒孩子要體諒外婆，不能一直賴著不肯回家。

母親愛用的廚具與難得的相聚時光

作者介紹母親最常使用的廚房用品：因為母親每天早上要吃早餐、服用藥物，所以很常使用鬆餅機的三明治烤盤，能同時烤麵包和煎蛋；她也喜歡一只外型漂亮的陶瓷鍋。那只鍋已經停產，是作者到韓國時收到的贈品，母親以前曾想帶回台灣，如今能在美國使用也很滿足。

母親難得來訪，作者盡量安排出遊，也趁有人幫忙照顧孩子時，和伴侶輪流處理積壓的工作，希望母親回去後生活能輕鬆一些。他們仍安排了幾趟附近旅行，例如到西雅圖參觀保育型動物園；園區保留大片自然環境，動物看起來像生活在野外。

追賞秋色，體驗南瓜季

母親此行最期待的是欣賞秋天的紅葉。作者一家住處周圍有各種顏色的樹葉，晴朗的天氣也讓母親每天散步都很愉快。他們走訪不同農場，讓孩子參加戶外活動，大人則在旁休息、挑選南瓜。作者一直想買南瓜裝飾家裡，這次終於趁母親同行，體驗了美國秋天的經典活動。

作者說明，秋天的南瓜不只是食物，也是重要的季節裝飾，有些品種甚至主要供擺設。家人挑選不同顏色與造型的南瓜，雖然外表不規則、看起來有點「醜」，卻很有萬聖節氣氛；這些南瓜買回家是用來裝飾，並不是打算吃掉。

萬聖節活動與孩子的裝扮難題

萬聖節前夕，當地動物園舉辦讓孩子穿著裝扮討糖的活動，作者帶母親一起參加，也展示父子倆的造型。接著，孩子學校舉行秋日慶典，附近農場也有萬聖節活動，穿著裝扮入場還能免費，因此一家人也前往參加。

作者特地準備了和孩子相配的服裝與頭飾，原本期待一家人完整變裝，沒想到孩子不願意穿，伴侶也不喜歡毛茸茸的服飾，精心準備的百元裝扮因此派不上用場。作者笑說，免費入場的吸引力很強，活動現場人潮遠比動物園更多；但為孩子挑衣服並不容易，男孩的選擇尤其有限。影片最後提到作者買了哈利波特造型服，後續內容則未在字幕中呈現。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 呈現三代同堂的日常分工，分享如何依照長輩的喜好相處，避免彼此勉強。
  • 記錄外婆陪伴孩子、協助家務的生活點滴，既溫馨又充滿幽默。
  • 帶領讀者感受美國秋日風景，從農場、南瓜到萬聖節活動，體驗當地季節氣氛。

摘要

三代同堂，各自分工

作者分享，母親已在家中住了兩個月，這段相處不是「血淚史」，而是溫馨的生活紀錄。作者認為有孩子後，三代同堂很值得推薦；不過，母親並不喜歡下廚或做家事，因此相處的關鍵是因材施教，按照她能接受的方式分配事情，不必要求她做不擅長、也不喜歡的工作。

平日早上，母親會陪孩子，白天則幫忙洗切蔬菜、整理碗盤、接孩子放學並帶他們出門玩。作者下班後只要專心準備晚餐，家務就能順利完成。作者打趣說，母親簡直像家中的「小幫手」，一家人各做各的，日子過得更有效率。

外婆陪玩，家人也心疼她

母親常帶孩子到公園散步、騎三輪車，還會陪他們放學後到處走走。孩子玩得開心，母親卻經常一出去就是一個多小時，甚至晚餐都準備好了還沒回家。作者和伴侶笑說，孩子已經懂得什麼時候可以使喚外婆，也擔心母親離開後，孩子會不習慣放學就直接回家。

為了慰勞辛苦散步回家的母親，家人準備了她喜歡的起司拼盤，還拿出幽靈、南瓜和蝙蝠造型的小叉子增添節日氣氛。母親回家後，作者也提醒孩子要體諒外婆，不能一直賴著不肯回家。

母親愛用的廚具與難得的相聚時光

作者介紹母親最常使用的廚房用品：因為母親每天早上要吃早餐、服用藥物，所以很常使用鬆餅機的三明治烤盤，能同時烤麵包和煎蛋；她也喜歡一只外型漂亮的陶瓷鍋。那只鍋已經停產，是作者到韓國時收到的贈品，母親以前曾想帶回台灣，如今能在美國使用也很滿足。

母親難得來訪，作者盡量安排出遊，也趁有人幫忙照顧孩子時，和伴侶輪流處理積壓的工作，希望母親回去後生活能輕鬆一些。他們仍安排了幾趟附近旅行，例如到西雅圖參觀保育型動物園；園區保留大片自然環境，動物看起來像生活在野外。

追賞秋色，體驗南瓜季

母親此行最期待的是欣賞秋天的紅葉。作者一家住處周圍有各種顏色的樹葉，晴朗的天氣也讓母親每天散步都很愉快。他們走訪不同農場，讓孩子參加戶外活動，大人則在旁休息、挑選南瓜。作者一直想買南瓜裝飾家裡，這次終於趁母親同行，體驗了美國秋天的經典活動。

作者說明，秋天的南瓜不只是食物，也是重要的季節裝飾，有些品種甚至主要供擺設。家人挑選不同顏色與造型的南瓜，雖然外表不規則、看起來有點「醜」，卻很有萬聖節氣氛；這些南瓜買回家是用來裝飾，並不是打算吃掉。

萬聖節活動與孩子的裝扮難題

萬聖節前夕，當地動物園舉辦讓孩子穿著裝扮討糖的活動，作者帶母親一起參加，也展示父子倆的造型。接著，孩子學校舉行秋日慶典，附近農場也有萬聖節活動，穿著裝扮入場還能免費，因此一家人也前往參加。

作者特地準備了和孩子相配的服裝與頭飾，原本期待一家人完整變裝，沒想到孩子不願意穿，伴侶也不喜歡毛茸茸的服飾，精心準備的百元裝扮因此派不上用場。作者笑說，免費入場的吸引力很強，活動現場人潮遠比動物園更多；但為孩子挑衣服並不容易，男孩的選擇尤其有限。影片最後提到作者買了哈利波特造型服，後續內容則未在字幕中呈現。
